# Bug Catalog: production deep-zone environment assets

**Generated by /design-tests on 2026-10-03**

## Public contract

- `res://art/deep_zone/Beach_assets1.fbx` is Glassgoat's approved source.
- Production may render its `Palm_Tree_1` mesh only; the bundled `Sand1` and
  `Water_1` test planes are not world scenery.
- Every admitted palm belongs to `deep_zone_tree` and is a visible,
  floor-aligned route-landmark accent outside the diver corridor.
- Existing `DeepZoneLayout.lab_route()` and `maze_route()` remain traversable.

## IO boundaries and branches

- Godot FBX import can lose the embedded palm texture or apply surprising
  source units.
- Runtime filtering must select one named mesh while excluding two sibling
  meshes from the same scene.
- Authored placement can make the trees technically present but tiny,
  floating, repetitive, or route-blocking.
- A headless invariant cannot decide whether underwater palms improve the
  composition; real-resolution captures remain a rejecting gate.

## Test design and self-critique

### DZ-ENV-001 and DZ-ENV-002

`deep-zone environment: approved palm imports and production excludes its
sand/water siblings — guards against missing art and giant test planes`
pins the exact delivered digest, visible textured palm, excluded sibling
names, and production group ownership. Digest pinning is justified because
the approved delivery is part of the contract. It does not judge placement.

### DZ-ENV-003 and DZ-ENV-004

`deep-zone environment: varied floor-aligned palms remain near landmarks and
outside both diver corridors — guards against tiny/floating/repetitive or
route-blocking scenery` checks observable world bounds and reuses the public
route-clearance contract. It does not pin scene-tree paths or exact transform
values.

### DZ-ENV-005

Automated checks cannot decide whether a palm cluster looks good. Normal
route captures at 1280×720 must show recognizable silhouettes, intentional
asymmetry, and no occlusion of the objective/entrance. A reviewer may reject
the placement even while all semantic gates pass.

## Skipped

- Sand and water integration: Glassgoat approved tree use; the game already
  owns its production floor/water treatment, so these source test planes are
  deliberately excluded.
- Tree collision: palms are decorative accents outside the route corridor;
  adding broad collision would create more navigation risk than value.
- Pixel snapshots: stable pixels are not proof of good composition.

## Post-write evaluation

- **Bugs caught:** DZ-ENV-001 first failed because the approved source was
  absent and no production palms existed. The first placement then exposed a
  unit-conversion bug: scales in the 48–60 range produced trees roughly
  870–1,015 world units high. Production scales of 0.35–0.44 yield readable
  6.34–7.97-unit silhouettes instead.
- **Bugs characterized:** DZ-ENV-002 proves the bundled `Sand1` and `Water_1`
  meshes stay hidden; DZ-ENV-003 proves four unique, floor-aligned placements
  remain near entry/maze landmarks; DZ-ENV-004 is green through the public
  lab and maze route-clearance gate.
- **Visual evaluation:** 1280×720 entry, maze, and lab frames show deliberate
  asymmetrical silhouettes, varied rocks, an unobstructed route, and the
  corrected hidden-lab door. Hosted-browser verification remains required.
